newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: National Mutual Life still bullish on costs.
newsitem.headline: National Mutual Life still bullish on costs.

text.p: Australian life office National Mutual Holding's local life subsidiary said on Tuesday it was making inroads in reducing its costs, despite its failure in the six months ended March to make a dent in capitalised losses.

National Mutual Life was the main contributer to group profit for the half-year announced on Tuesday, but it was also mainly responsible for A$8 million in capitalised losses in the half, as it struggled with competition for its risk products.
National Mutual Holdings still reported a net write-back of capitalised losses of A$12 million in the half-year, due to better information available to assess those losses.
"The risk products ares is one area that's really hurting us at the present time and we are finding stiff competition," said National Mutual Life managing director Tony Killen.
Capitalised losses now amount to about A$100 million.
Killen said he was confident these could be written back over the next two years with further attacks on costs.
"There is about A$100 million we think are capable of being reversed over the next couple of years," he told reporters.
Reversals of capitalised losses flow to the bottom line.
"Our objective over the balance of this year (ending September 30) is to continue to put pressure on costs and build volumes," Killen said.

National Mutual Life is fighting a price war on its risk products -- in the areas of term, trauma and income protection -- from rivals such as the Australian Mutual Provident Society and Mercantile Mutual.
National Mutual Life plans to introduce a new range of risk products on July 1 as a response to the price war, Killen said.
But, he added, "We will only go so far (on price) to responding to competition."
Killen said the half-year figures masked a broader, underlying progress in National Mutual Life's level of costs.
"The true position is masked a bit. Last year we had 25 of our products making losses," he said.
"In the first half, we reduced that to 17 so in effect we have converted eight product groups from loss to profit, so there's been some improvement in our position..."
National Mutual Life earned A$110.8 million after tax in the half-year. The group's half-year profit rose 18 percent to A$175.52.
